- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.6) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next period.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >10% from prior period), model often overshoots; apply a 3–7 day lag correction, dampening forecast by 10–20% in the following 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.3) and prices are trending down, model frequently underestimates; adjust upward by 3–8% to capture mean reversion.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often fails to capture short-term volatility; if sentiment swings sharply, reduce forecast horizon sensitivity to sentiment changes.
- When sentiment is mixed or near-zero, model tends to average out; use sentiment-weighted smoothing: higher sentiment = higher weight on recent price, lower sentiment = lower weight on recent price.
- If model forecast is >15% above true outcome for 3 consecutive days, apply downward bias correction: subtract 1–3% per day until convergence.
- If model forecast is <10% below true outcome for 3 consecutive days, apply upward bias correction: add 1–3% per day until convergence.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often overestimates early in the horizon; apply a 1–2 day decay factor to reduce weight of early forecast points.
